subject: Quick question about specifying location when using DSM

messages.author: 9a19b1e1528f7677
messages.subject: Quick question about specifying location when using DSM
parts:
Hi, just a quick question about how the location of segments and prediction grids is specified in the Density Surface Modelling package.

Is it the case that regardless of whether point counts or transects are used, segment records (and prediction grids) must be located at an x and y coordinate (i.e. the dsm package can't take sf linestrings/polygons etc. as a location column)

eg I've got some bird transect data recorded in 200m segments & I've used sf to create 200x200m sf.polygons for each segment, and have a 200x200m prediction grid of sf.polygons across the study area (necessary to get mean environmental covariates across the 200x200m space where observations are made). 

My understanding is that to run dsm with my data I must make sure that the segdata and preddata dataframes have columns named 'x' and 'y' with the coordinates at the centroid of each polygon?

An additional question (if my understanding above is correct) would be whether you're considering having the dsm package take sf geometry columns as a location argument in the dataframes in future?

Thanks!
David

My understanding of the workings of dsm​ match yours; x- and y-coordinates are used for segment centroids and prediction grid cell coordinates. Regarding future enhancements to dsm​  using sf​ geometry, I defer to Dave Miller for his response.
